data.why: The repo already commits its own example dataset (pesquisa/dados/soja_para_painel.csv, municipios_para.csv, para_geo.json, rios_para.json, eventos_enso.json, conab/levantamento_atual.json) and app.py loads them via fixed relative paths from its own folder, so nothing needs to be copied, uploaded, or synthesized.

goals: Pick a Para municipality and see its predicted soybean yield for the next season, with the declared error margin (kg/ha or sacas/ha)
Compare the predicted yield against the official historical PAM/IBGE series, noticing which harvest years repeat the prior year's value (a data-quality flag)
Simulate a climate scenario (rainfall and temperature) for the season and observe how little it moves the yield estimate, which is the dissertation's central finding
Browse the state map of producing municipalities sized by planted area and colored by recent yield, comparing the selected municipality against another
Estimate total production (tons and sacas) and the economic outcome per hectare (revenue minus cost margin), editing the CONAB-sourced price and cost assumptions
Download the municipality's series or the full dataset as CSV for further analysis

review.summary: The tree matches the README's purpose closely: forecast with its error margin, check that the official record repeats values, show that weather barely moves the estimate, compute the per-hectare margin, and export CSV. Every screen I checked supports its node. It needs small fixes before filing: a broken feature-to-task link, a projection card that silently follows the farm-expectation input, the 'model adds about 1 kg/ha over trend' note left out, and an over-bundled f2.
